candidates.locator: Page 16, Section: statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, B. 40 CFR CITATIONS
candidates.exact_span:
Citations to 40 CFR are as of December 6, 2013.
Sections 122, 124, 125, 133, 136
candidates.computation_change_reason: The as-of date fixes which regulatory text version was used to develop the permit; Sections 133 and 136 in particular can govern effluent-limit derivation and monitoring/method requirements. A different reading of the controlling CFR version or which cited parts are operative could change which numeric limits are treated as enforceable (A) and which monitoring rules apply (B).

candidates.locator: Page 16, Section: statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, C. STATE OF NEW MEXICO REFERENCES
candidates.exact_span:
New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Water, 20.6.4 NMAC,
effective, effective July 24, 2020.
candidates.computation_change_reason: State surface-water standards are a cited basis for permit limit development; interpreting the effective date (including the duplicated 'effective') or which NMAC edition controls could change which water-quality-based numeric discharge limits are considered applicable in FY2025 comparisons.

candidates.locator: Page 16, Section: statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, C. STATE OF NEW MEXICO REFERENCES
candidates.exact_span: State of New Mexico 303(d) List for Assessed Stream and River Reaches, 2014 - 2016.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cited 303(d) listing vintage can bear on whether receiving-water impairment triggers more stringent or additional water-quality-based limits; different interpretation of which list period is controlling could change the enforceable numeric limits selected for comparison.

candidates.locator: Page 16, Section: statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, C. STATE OF NEW MEXICO REFERENCES
candidates.exact_span: Procedures for Implementing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Permits in New Mexico, March 15, 2012.
candidates.computation_change_reason: State NPDES implementation procedures are listed as a permit-development authority; interpreting whether and how this March 2012 procedure document governs monitoring frequency, conditional monitoring, or special-study triggers could change which monitoring obligations are deemed applicable for FY2025.

candidates.locator: Page 16, Section: statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, A. APPLICATION(s)
candidates.exact_span:
EPA Application Form 1 and 2C received on April 13, 2021. Additional Permit application
information were received on August 26, 2021; August 20, 2021; July 29, 2021; July 20, 2021;
July 8, 2021; June 30, 2021; June 21, 2021; and May 13, 2021. The application was deemed
administratively complete on July 8, 2021.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These dates anchor which application materials and completeness milestone were used to formulate permit terms. Interpreting which submission set is controlling, or when the application became complete, could change the permit obligations treated as in force for FY2025—including applicable limits (A), monitoring schedules and conditions (B), and what evidentiary baseline exists when reported results are absent (C).

candidates.locator: Page 16, Section: statement_of_basis, XVII. ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD, D. MISCELLANEOUS REFERENCES
candidates.exact_span:
Email from Andrew Galloway, Chief Operator, Aztec Water Treatment Plant to Maria Okpala,
EPA, dated August 26, 2021; August 23, 2021; August 9, 2021; July 29, 2021; July 20, 2021;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Operator-to-agency emails are listed as part of the administrative record that may document discharge occurrence, no-discharge periods, or explanations for missing data. Whether these communications are treated as establishing a documented no-data or no-discharge state versus leaving gaps unresolved could change missing-evidence classification for FY2025 monitoring expectations without ordinary numeric results.
